speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am pleased with the recent housing policy announcements that make housing more accessible to more diverse groups of Singaporeans whilst also enhancing the subsidy schemes that strive to make our housing system a fair one.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I would like to address our public rental housing and to highlight the potential we have of transforming it and harnessing it to catalyse the social mobility of our lowest income Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In recent years, the Ministry of National Development (MND) has taken the step to incorporate and integrate rental flats into build-To-order (BTO) purchase blocks, such as the ones in Marsiling and Bukit Batok.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This is a bold move that I support.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I know itis not an easy decision, as I am aware that there are pockets of Singaporeans who hold quite contrary views and who are concerned that having rental units within their blocks could cause a devaluation of their flats.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Nevertheless, I am glad the Government chose to do the right thing by prioritising social mixing and integration over political popularity.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This addresses the larger social good, especially with emerging trends and threats of social polarisation along class lines that our society is facing.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: All Singaporeans need to support this effort, if we truly believe that each one of us are our brother's keepers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: To uplift those struggling with their lives, there is more our public rental housing can do beyond just providing a roof over heads.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In my speech today, I make a case for enhancing public rental housing to enable human thriving.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In past Parliament Sittings, I sought statistics from the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and MND on how long it takes for the average rental housing family to move out to their own purchased flats.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: My hon colleague Ms Mariam Jaafer also sought information on the rate of transition by rental flat families to their own homes in the last five years.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We can do this by reimagining and redesigning rental flats to help occupants unlock their full potential.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I invite this House to go on a design thinking journey with me to understand how space and aesthetics in our living environment actually have a profound impact on human functioning and thereby can aid with social mobility.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: From my conversations with healthcare providers at Woodlands Health Campus and Yishun Health, which we collaborate with in the community, data from our healthcare system shows that lower-income residents tend to be "frequent flyers" at hospitals.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The phenomenon of 20% of healthcare users taking up the majority of healthcare expenses is not uncommon.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We can understand that one factor leading to poor health is overcrowding and another is stress.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Infections spread easily amongst family members in cramped environments and poor hygiene in common spaces can facilitate disease across households.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Poorer health leads to poor employment retention and more frequent school absences.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: MSF is very familiar with these challenges – high rates of employment turnover and disproportionately higher rates of school absenteeism amongst children from rental blocks communities.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The common and perplexing challenge many social service agencies face seems to be – how come the poor seem to be less motivated?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If we pause to think about it, might it not be because they are struggling more in their day-to-day lives due to basic, bare-bone and often stressful living conditions which they do not have the resources to improve on their own?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Home becomes a place just to survive but not to thrive in.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We under-estimate the amount of energy it takes to overcome challenges inherent in the current rental housing premises, leaving less energy for constructive actions, such as focusing on job performance or school performance.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Let us look squarely at just one such challenge observed in our rental estates – overcrowding.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It is not uncommon when I do my house visits to come across families with three, four, sometimes five children living in a 2-room flat.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Having people live in insufficient spaces makes it difficult to keep common spaces tidy.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Household and personal belongings tend to spill out into common corridors, creating obstruction and potential hazards.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: These then create tensions with neighbours and among family members, adding on stress from conflict in their day-to-day lives.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Many Town Councils and the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) regularly receive feedback on fire hazards and end up having to manage neighbourly disputes that are hard to resolve because people simply do not have sufficient space for their daily activities, such as their laundry, their clothes racks, their shoes.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Such neighbourly tensions make for very poor quality of life for residents and also create unnecessary toll on public resources.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Another important side effect of overcrowding is on children's development.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, immense challenges were faced by children in rental flats trying to cope with home-based learning in limited space.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In a community collaboration that Nee Soon South had with Yishun Health and SportSG, it was observed by volunteers in a football programme for children from rental block families that the kids had poorer hand-eye coordination and could not throw or catch as well as other kids.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We suspect that space constraints had a role in limiting the amount of play within flats, compromising the psychomotor development of children who live in cramped spaces.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: One can imagine that children living in such tiny flats are very much curtailed in their play.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: They cannot really throw a ball to their sibling at home without the risk of hitting something or getting yelled at by a frustrated parent.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: How can we expect children to study, play, learn and grow up well physically, emotionally and mentally in such conditions?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Next, I would like to talk about the role of aesthetics in human potential.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: From the earliest philosophers to modern-day psychologists, scholars and researchers have recognised the power of beauty to inspire and motivate us.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Research in psychology has shown that exposure to beautiful environments can have a positive impact on our mental health and well-being.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: For example, a study published in the Journal of Environmental Psychology found that people who worked in aesthetically pleasing environments were more productive and had a greater sense of well-being than those who worked in less aesthetically pleasing environments.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, aesthetics can also inspire us to be our best selves.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Art can help us to see the world in new and different ways, challenging our perspectives and inspiring us to be more empathetic, compassionate and socially responsible.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: What we can infer logically is that just focusing on objective functionality alone, without considering the value of aesthetics is to miss an opportunity – to inspire and catalyse empathy, compassion and an increased sense of civic responsibility in rental housing communities.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If one pays attention, it is not hard to notice that the general cleanliness upkeep in rental estates is much more challenging than those in purchased estates.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: What is commonly observed are higher rates of high-rise littering, misuse or poor use of common chutes, dirty common corridors and void decks.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Most Town Councils share a common challenge in having to deploy more cleaning and maintenance resources in rental block areas.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I say this not to shame rental block residents but for us to really investigate what the causes and reasons behind such behaviours are.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: They reveal little willingness or motivation in occupants to help upkeep and maintain common spaces.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Is this function simply because of a lack of ownership because the flats do not belong to them?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If that is so, how then do we explain the behavior of much more cooperative behavior when people stay at hotels?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We do not own the premises in hotels but we do not also commonly hear of people trashing hotel rooms or littering at hotel lobbies and premises even though the people who stay there are temporary occupants.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This begs a deeper examination into the factors contributing to civic behaviour.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: What common sense tells us is that the common behavior and attitude of people towards places and things that are beautiful and pleasing is that we are naturally inclined to want to keep them that way.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: As the philosopher Immanuel Kant once aptly said, "Beauty is a symbol of morality." Beauty has the power to evoke and inspire the higher qualities and virtues in human beings.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: When we are exposed to beauty, we are more likely to feel motivated to pursue our goals with greater determination and to push ourselves to be our best selves.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: One of them is the first shelter project in Oregon that uses trauma-informed design by a non-profit called Path Home.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Here, Mr Speaker, I would like to show a visual example of what their shelter for the homeless looks like.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The founder of Path Home shared in an interview that the design was "based on research done since the 1960s in hospitals, looking into what kinds of facilities promote better reactions among patients. "Some of the key elements they’ve identified include having a connection to nature – lots of light, real plants indoors and outdoors – and building with natural materials, so they used a lot of real wood.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The color palette is also very calming – lots of greens and turquoises from the ocean." The founder also said, "It’s about helping families feel worthy (so) that they can get up and do the hard work to get their lives back on track." This project has had much success and positive feedback from its inhabitants.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It demonstrates the role of aesthetics in uplifting the human spirit and catalysing human motivation.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We under-estimate just how being able to have something beautiful can uplift an individual's sense of self-esteem and fundamentally shift their self-perception and motivation.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We see the same principle across many makeover TV shows across different cultures, TV shows where a makeover has the power to change someone's life by changing how they perceive themselves.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: There is also a global architecture firm called the Workplace Group at HOK that has created a landmark guidebook on trauma-informed design with the goal of helping people to quiet the part of the brain that stays in survival mode.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Research has shown that the positive emotional effect of the aesthetic experience affects mood and indirectly promotes health and well-being.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: These benefits include improvement of memory, lower stress levels and increased social connection.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: By using design to enhance living spaces with aesthetics, colours, lighting and art, instead of inhabitants coming home feeling fearful and on high alert from a difficult day, chronically operating on flight or fight mode, they can be more relaxed when they return home, which has proven to improve executive functioning.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: This can help them focus better on actions like applying for jobs or getting their children to school.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: This belief, long held by too many in the system, that providing a pleasing and comfortable environment for public rental housing residents might demotivate them from working hard to move out, also really needs to change.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: These are limiting beliefs that curtail the possibilities and potential of our own citizens who are striving hard to improve their lives.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We can do more for the Singaporeans who need our utmost support to help them overcome the adversities in their lives.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: And having aesthetically pleasing homes, with just sufficient space for inhabitants to participate in daily activities stress-free, is akin to having an ever-present cheerleader that one can come home to everyday.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Instead of assuming and blaming lack of personal motivation for poor social mobility outcomes, let us take a more scientific and proactive approach to study the environmental factors that we can enhance to improve human motivation and potential.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I recognise that in these fiscally challenging times, cost is always a consideration.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Instead of increasing costs, there are ways we can rethink the design and construction of rental housing to optimise the value of expenditure we are already planning to spend on rental housing provision.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Furthermore, any incremental costs could have a disproportionate positive return in terms of wellbeing and savings in longer-term healthcare and welfare spending.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The long-term gains may well outweigh the short-term incremental costs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Architects and design thinkers know full well how design influences and shapes human behaviour.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We must recognise the importance of space and beauty in our lives and strive to create environments that inspire and enable human thriving.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: By doing so, we can unlock the full potential of our rental housing families and give them that much more – a better starting point to recover and thrive from their adversities.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The Government does not need to do this alone.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The co-living pilot refurbished from the old Anderson Junior College hostel was well intended but implementation fell too far short.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We can do better, so let us do it together.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We share Ms Tan's belief in the power and social impact of good design.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As the master planner and developer of Singapore's public housing estates, HDB appreciates the importance of quality homes and environments that enhance residents' wellbeing and support Singaporeans to lead their best lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To that end, HDB launched its "Designing for Life" roadmap in 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The roadmap seeks to enhance residents' physical, mental and social well-being through thoughtful, resident-centred design, for example, by bringing nature and greenery closer to residents, improving facilities for active living and providing ample community spaces to encourage social connections.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Rental flats are always built as part of a wider HDB neighbourhood.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This means that rental tenants enjoy the same communal facilities and amenities as sold flat owners, including community living rooms, roof gardens, fitness facilities, playgrounds, neighbourhood shops, preschool centres and Active Ageing Centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the years, we have made progressive improvements to our rental flats to enhance their design and provide a better living environment for our tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Rental blocks that were built since 2007 are better designed with enhanced natural lighting and ventilation within units and at the corridors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These newer blocks are very different from the older rental blocks that have long corridors with units lined on both sides.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition, we have been building public rental flats alongside sold flats – in the same projects and, since 2014, in the same blocks and on the same floors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In integrated blocks such as those at Marsiling Greenview and West Plains @ Bukit Batok, public rental flats look no different from sold flats from the outside.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: On the inside, they have similar finishes and fittings as 2-room Flexi sold flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We do this because having a good social mix is a key objective of our public housing programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After the first integrated block was completed at Marsiling Greenview, we commissioned a study with the National University of Singapore to understand the impact of this integrated design.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We found that the design features have encouraged interactions and ties between owners and tenants, for example, by locating sold flats and rental flats on the same floor, minimising visible differences between sold flats, and rental flats and having shared amenities such as playgrounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The study also found that owners and tenants have the same perceptions of what constitutes a liveable environment and they act in similar ways to uphold these standards, for example, in terms of upkeeping shared corridor spaces and managing cleanliness.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are encouraged by these findings and will apply these learnings to the design of future integrated blocks.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also explore new typologies to improve the living environment for public rental tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The SRSF aims to give tenants greater privacy while providing shared facilities to prevent social isolation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Each tenant will have their own private bedroom that comes with basic furnishings such as a bedframe, table and wardrobe.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Amenities like toilets, kitchens, dining areas and laundry rooms will be shared to ensure that we make good use of the space and to facilitate social interaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For older public rental blocks, HDB keeps them in good condition through regular maintenance and upgrading.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Older rental blocks will typically be upgraded together with sold blocks when the entire area is rejuvenated through HDB's various upgrading programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also progressively redeveloping older clusters of rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Tenants who are relocated can move to newer rental flats with improved designs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We empathise with Ms Tan's point about providing a good living environment for rental families with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have been making efforts in this area and will seek to further improve the design of flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under the Public Rental Scheme, HDB generally offers 1- and 2-room flats to cater to both singles and families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The vast majority of our public rental households – more than nine in 10 – have four or fewer persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We do not have a hard space norm per person but we recognise that some larger households may have space concerns and have already started some efforts to help provide a better environment for families with young children, including using good design to overcome the constraints of land and space.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These are typically sized similarly to 2-room Flexi sold flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The space can be used as a child's room with a single bed and a small wardrobe, or as a study or activity room to support children's development.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For larger families, those able to form two family nuclei will be allocated two public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Where possible, HDB strives to ensure that both flats are located near each other to facilitate mutual care and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB also works with MSF to offer 3-room public rental flats to selected large families with children on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Like Ms Tan, we are driven by the desire to see families achieving social mobility and seniors ageing well even if they live in public rental.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: But to achieve these, hardware alone is insufficient.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We need to pair hardware with good social support and programming to make concerted efforts to address households' needs and aspirations holistically.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, HDB works with relevant people sector partners to support seniors in public rental flats with active ageing programmes and assisted living services.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At a rental block in Kebun Baru, the Integrated Dementia Assisted Living project by Dementia Singapore offers a telehealth room, community kitchen and social programming to support seniors living in the rental block to age well in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For families with young children living in public rental flats, Government agencies and community partners work closely together through the ComLink+ programme to provide coordinated support.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: ComLink officers and Family Coaches will journey with families, understand their needs and aspirations and work with them to develop goals and action plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Different agencies and partners then work together backend, behind the scenes, to support families' individual needs – the Ministry of Education for school subsidies, the Ministry of Health for healthcare, Family Service Centres for family counselling, community-based after-school care and programmes for children, and so on.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In Boon Lay, for example, children in ComLink+ families may spend their after-school hours at the Tak Takut Kids Club.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The club is operated by 3Pumpkins, a community-based organisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Located at the ground floor of a rental block, it runs various free play, sports and crafts activities, and provides a safe and supportive environment where children can grow and express themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Once families apply for a public rental flat and are assessed to be eligible, they will automatically be enrolled in ComLink+.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A ComLink officer will then proactively reach out to them to offer support even before they move into their rental flat and continue to journey with them as they work towards achieving stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When public rental families achieve stability and build up their finances, we support them on their journey towards homeownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I have met many rental families and I know that many of them hope to buy their own flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We provide substantial housing grants for lower-income families on top of the significant subsidies that we provide for all BTO flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First-timers can tap on the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant and receive up to $80,000 while second-timers can tap on the $15,000 Step-Up CPF Housing Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also have the Fresh Start Housing Scheme, which helps second-timer families with young children living in public rental flats to own a home again.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There is also a dedicated Home ownership Support Team at HDB, who will provide one-to-one guidance to tenants on their homebuying journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The team will share practical tips and advice on their housing budget and options and guide families through the process of flat selection, application and booking.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Khairi and Mdm Dayang is one of them.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, you have a minute left.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Together with their five children, they moved into their new home earlier this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Before that, they had been living in public rental for some years.
